extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing the professional conduct, suspension, reinstatement, probation, and sanctions for persons practicing patent/trademark law before the USPTO under the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and related regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on practicing while suspended (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may not engage in the practice of patent (or other) law before the Office while suspended from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of prohibited conduct include discussing patent law/procedure with prospective applicants and preparing and filing patent applications while suspended (the Final Order cites Respondent's discussing patent law on or about January 22, 2009, and preparing/filing utility applications on May 8, 2009 and September 29, 2009).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify clients of significant correspondence (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8) / §§ 10.23(a),(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must notify clients of correspondence he receives on their behalf where (a) the correspondence could have had a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office and (b) a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances that the clients should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to notify in such circumstances is sanctioned (the Order finds at least five occasions where Respondent did not notify clients of such correspondence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of diligence / prohibition on neglect leading to abandonment (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must not neglect patent applications such that they become abandoned without the clients' knowledge or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect resulting in abandonment is actionable (the Order finds at least two occasions where Respondent's neglect caused abandonment). This standard supports findings of misconduct and can lead to suspension/probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to refund unearned fees / client property (37 C.F.R. § 10.40(a) referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must refund fees paid for services not performed and otherwise safeguard client property; restitution may be required as a condition of reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites a $300 fee paid to Respondent for preparing/filing an application that was never done and states Respondent must refund $300 and that the OED may require proof of restitution when seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with suspension notification/administrative obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner must comply with the administrative obligations imposed by the suspension rules (e.g., notification requirements) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires Respondent to comply with § 11.58 for the new suspension and for the prior suspension; noncompliance can trigger further proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement timing and procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner may file a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; the Final Order permits filing for reinstatement after twelve months from the date the Final Order is signed (seeking reinstatement effective prior to expiration of the full suspension period is addressed by regulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED may bar a respondent from filing for reinstatement under certain circumstances; proof of compliance with obligations (e.g., restitution) may be required for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation terms and enforcement process
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may be placed on probation following suspension, during which the OED Director monitors compliance and may initiate enforcement actions if the practitioner fails to comply with the Final Order or Disciplinary Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order imposes a 48-month probation. If the OED Director believes the practitioner violated the Final Order or rules during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the respondent's last address of record, grant 15 days to respond, and may deliver arguments/evidence to the USPTO Director requesting barring of reinstatement or additional suspension (up to 24 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential dissociation from USPTO accounts and PKI upon additional disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director bars reinstatement or additionally suspends the practitioner, the Office shall dissociate the practitioner's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates and the practitioner may not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a collateral administrative consequence of further disciplinary action and is triggered by the Director's order following OED proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders and disciplinary notices are published in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette, with notices materially consistent with the Order's language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs publication of the Final Order at the OED Reading Room (providing the URL) and publication of a notice in the Official Gazette summarizing the suspension, probation, and factual basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings and as aggravating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of the disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) in future complaints or proceedings concerning the respondent, either as an aggravating factor in determining discipline or to rebut statements made on the practitioner's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in the Agreement/Final Order prevents the Office from relying on this record in subsequent disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional and statutory authority for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director exercises jurisdiction under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to approve settlement agreements and impose discipline under the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (Part 10 of 37 C.F.R.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the statutory/regulatory bases for the proceedings and for the Director's authority to approve the settlement and enter disciplinary orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, each party (the OED Director and the respondent) shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement/Final Order expressly states that the OED Director and Respondent each bear their own costs.
